title: Reading a LaserScan
description: What the ranges array holds, and how it becomes points on screen.

steps.title: A list of distances
steps.body:
A `LaserScan` is mostly one array: **`ranges`**, a distance in metres for each direction the scanner looked, one after another.

Here there are 360 of them, one per degree, starting at `angle_min` and stepping by `angle_increment`. `range_max` is how far it can see. A value of `inf` means "nothing came back".

steps.title: Distances become points
steps.body:
Entry number `i` points in the direction `angle_min + i * angle_increment`. A distance `r` in that direction is the point `(r cos a, r sin a)`.

The 3D view does exactly that for all 360 entries, in the scanner's own frame, then places the ring with TF.

steps.title: One slice versus many
steps.body:
The 2D scanner sees one flat ring, low on the robot. The 3D LiDAR on the left of this pair sweeps 16 rings at different heights.

Both are LiDARs. A `LaserScan` is the compact form for a flat scanner; a `PointCloud2` is the general form.
